data_description.baichuan_deep_start: When a start or a seek lands well past what is cached of a recording, ask the device for that moment directly (its own protocol, port 9000) instead of downloading everything before it. The first picture shows in about a second, and the recording is copied in two pieces, nothing twice. Adds one logged-in user on the device while in use. Falls back to the download on any failure; a device that refuses the protocol is not asked again for 6 hours.
data_description.learn_normal: Keep a journal of what each camera detects (people, vehicles, animals, motion, doorbell presses) and when, so Reolink Viewer can learn what is normal for each camera and mark what is unusual. The journal shows when your cameras see people, and so when the house is empty: it stays in a file on this Home Assistant (reolink_viewer_journal.db, in the config folder), included in its backups, and is never sent anywhere. Turning this off deletes it, and so does removing Reolink Viewer. It starts with the last 10 days of Home Assistant's own history of these sensors.
data_description.unusual_sensitivity: Unusual means rare for that camera, never dangerous: a burglar in a busy driveway at 3 pm is not unusual. A camera marks once it has a week of history and 200 detections.
data_description.unusual_scope: Each camera is judged against its own past first. This decides what a camera with little history may borrow from, and which cameras count as having fired just before another.
data_description.unusual_signals: Optional. States from around the house that say something a camera cannot: anyone home, the alarm, a gate or door lock, the camera's day/night state, the light outside. Each detection is learned with what they stood at, so a person on the drive with everyone away can stand out where the same person with someone home does not. Their last days come from Home Assistant's history; the cameras' own detection sensors are not offered.
data_description.event_clip_before: "Save event" on the Playback page saves an MP4 of the event playing. It starts this long before the event, at the key frame just before that.
data_description.event_clip_after: How long the saved clip goes on after the event ends. A clip stays within the recording its event is in.

options.balanced: Balanced (a few a day at most)
options.many: More, including borderline ones (about 6 a day at most)
